The sill node's F8 / F9 / F14 get their sealed inline holders now, fitted empty — every future circuit ends in a holder or half a connector, none bare
The engine leg is built for the FB/FC alternator only; every other alternator is provided for at the fuse/relay/PMU end, never as wire in the bay
Future circuits run both conductors down the leg and branch only what the fitted part needs; the wiper park sense is the first case
CAN never leaves the dashboard: no rear node, no engine-bay drop, and every computer including a future ECU is a dash node
The master disconnect returns to the positive side: one switch at the battery carrying both the PMU leg and the starter leg
The kick-down is reproduced and stays operational
The starter MRBF goes to 250 A, sized to the 1/0 cable it protects
Limp-home is the config file and a USB-to-CAN cable carried in the car plus a one-page written emergency procedure
Nothing is bought until the design is complete and Camden understands it; no cart is paid early
The heated washer nozzle and the wiper-park de-icer are cancelled; L2-S 6 and the L2-NZL receptacle come out. The outside-air conductor is untouched
Battery data comes from the Ionic BMS over BLE; no shunt is bought, and current and state of charge wait on the protocol
The master disconnect is the Blue Sea 9004e; its auxiliary pole is a switch-position input so the PMU drops excitation before the main contacts break
The PMU-24 DL's channel set is complete - sixteen analog channels, six of them running as outputs, and not one position spare
Output health is a band around a measured baseline, and the low half of it is the module's own undercurrent flag
Retry is four named classes, and the pop-up bus is the one that must not retry
The PMU cannot report an output stuck ON; it is inferred from output voltage against output state and it can only annunciate
The PMU publishes no quiescent current, so D-280's measurement is the only number there will ever be
The PMU has a native delayed turn-off; the keep-alive expression may move into it, the wiring does not
Two routing rules the benchmark earned: water enters from below or not at all, and the tach shield never runs beside a coil lead
Two conventions written down: a cavity number is the moulding, and the fuse-lid card is a query
The bundle-derating audit changes nothing, because no conductor in this harness is loaded above 10 A continuous
Route lengths become a measured table; the wire schedule and W-329 wait on M-2 rather than on another estimate
The kick-down gets its own inline fuse off the ignition output and three conductors, and rides the tunnel run that is already there
The limp-home procedure is a table inside the record, and the glovebox kit is three parts
The ICU's battery frames carry voltage only, and a field with no source is left undefined rather than published as zero
CAN2's second terminator is at the dash node
The pack's own limits go into 00-CAR, and the factory charging band's top sits above them
T-017 is done: the design's factory terminal letters are right, and reading the scans found three things that are not
The project directories are renamed 00-electrical / 01-luxury / 02-engine, the directory name is the area's identity, and the decision bodies keep the old paths on purpose
The control panel is the DCU's faceplate, not its own board: DP-KEY and L3-WIN are deleted, DP-DCU gets a constant feed and a wake line, and parked behaviour becomes a PMU gate
The master-switch position sense is dropped and its conductor with it; the disconnect goes back to the simpler 9003e and the TVS stands alone
The fuel pump gets a series relay off the ignition switch, K13, as the one mechanical back-stop against a shorted-on output
The dead-module limp keeps two feeds, not three: the brake-lamp feed is dropped rather than run constant, and beacons go in the bag instead
No PMU output is free, so the release solenoids stay on O10 and ACCESSORY gains a self-clearing release term
Blocks are numbered per project, <prefix>.<n>; every BLK- id is renamed
MOTOR_BUS takes a conditional retry class: guarded during a pop-up cycle, motor during a window command
The mirrors share one clutch line: four DCU lines on L3-S3 5–8, the clutch spliced at the post onto both mirrors
cad/ holds a step-by-step layout and 3D guide for both carriers, and board layout is no longer fenced out
Window relays K5–K8 are two textbook reversing pairs: motor leg on 30, fused feed on 87, 87a and 85 to ground; the DCU drives 86 high-side
The limp-home fuel-pump feed lands on K13 terminal 30, so the key still switches the pump
A3, A6 and A8 get 47 kΩ baselines at the far end, as A4/A5 have, so at rest is a reading and open is a fault
Mirror heat is switched high-side by the DCU, as D-254 meant: L4-P 4 is fed from the DCU, not the O15 splice
The DCU picks hatch or fuel door by grounding K3's or K4's coil during the O10 release pulse
The BT817 evaluation board is the one exception to D-323: it is bought now, as a design tool
Install steps are work rows in stage E, one per step, gated in order - no install table
Each project gets a generated, read-only TODO.md from its work table - the second generated document

The ICU and the DCU are both this build's, whole: boards, channels, enclosures, connectors, firmware, the panel's electronics and the bus map; the luxury package keeps only the loads the DCU drives and the plastics
The door and A8 wake stages are pulse (edge) stages: one 1 µF film capacitor per side, so a door left ajar wakes the PMU once and cannot hold it on
ECUMaster's PMU client runs on the existing Windows laptop, kept as a car tool only; the project and all development stay on the Fedora machine

The ICU carrier's Teensy 4.1 pin map: CAN1 on 22/23, the tach and road speed on FreqMeasureMulti pins 2 and 3, the BT817 on single-lane SPI0 (10-13, PDN 9), and every channel promoted into icu_channels.teensy_pin
The PMU's frames 0x100-0x130 are a CANbus Export we define, not a layout ECUMaster fixes; fail-open is a per-input default and on-timeout value
The DCU carrier's parts check (V-083): protected low-side switches for the seats, 65 V-rated high-side switches, one quad half-bridge for the mirrors, and a 5 A buck for the servo rail
The control panel's electronics: nine keys on a diode-isolated 3 × 3 matrix, four detented encoders, the thumbstick, all on one 20-way IDC ribbon to the DCU
The door and A8 wake stages' values: excitation 220k switched off while awake, sense divider 1M / 560k, a 1 µF edge into a follower, pulse about 0.4 s - all confirm until CK12
The DCU's comfort circuits: 7.5 A per seat heater, 5 A per seat cooler, 5 A for mirror heat, and an 8-way DT13 comfort connector with its own two ground pins
Each harness leg gets two generated drawings - a pin ladder (A) and a route map (B) - under 00-electrical/diagrams, rebuilt by rx7.py diagrams; the four options are kept for a later switch

The electrical project splits into 00-design and 01-build, each with its own generated TODO; nothing in build starts before the design is reviewed and frozen (phase SOURCING); the 2026-09-23 risk review becomes work and blocks

The car comes apart once: the design list ends with the interior stripped (all wiring left in place) and the measurements that need it out; the build list starts from the interior out and ends with it back in
Planning is open in every project at every phase: the phase says how far the build has got, never whether design may be touched
